sources.note: GRBL pin layout image (pre-0.9 mapping), V3.XX schematic (shield header to Uno pin wiring, A-axis jumpers to X/Y/Z or D12/D13, 12-36V input), version history (V3.10 adds GRBL 0.9 PWM spindle support).

summary: Four-axis stepper shield for the Arduino Uno running GRBL. Takes four A4988/DRV8825-style drivers; X, Y, Z have their own pins and A clones an axis or uses D12/D13.

warnings.text: The pin functions depend on the GRBL version. GRBL 0.9/1.1 default builds (variable spindle PWM) swap two pins compared with GRBL 0.8c and the shield silkscreen: D11 (shield "Z+/Z-" end-stop pins) becomes the spindle PWM/enable output, and D12 (shield "SpnEn" pin) becomes the Z limit input. This table shows the GRBL 1.1 default; the 0.8c use is in each pin's notes. A5 is the probe input in GRBL 0.9/1.1 only.

The A axis has no Uno pins of its own. Jumpers on the shield set A.STEP/A.DIR to clone the X, Y or Z step/dir signals (A moves together with that axis, e.g. a dual-motor gantry), or connect them to D12 (A.STEP) and D13 (A.DIR). Stock GRBL does not drive a 4th axis on D12/D13, and on GRBL 0.9/1.1 D12 is the Z limit, so that option needs different firmware.
Motor power (12-36 V per the shield silkscreen) goes into the screw terminal, not through the Uno.
The shield E-Stop pins connect to the Uno RESET line (same as pressing the Uno reset button). Protoneer recommends a real emergency stop that cuts power to the machine as well.

Board marked unverified because the Protoneer page (only reachable as an archived copy) documents the pre-0.9 mapping. The GRBL 1.1 mapping comes from GRBL cpu_map.h and the GRBL wiki. Each pin has been checked against both sources.

pins.label: D0
pins.notes: Serial link to the host (G-code sender). Broken out on the shield RX/TX header. Leave free.

pins.label: D1
pins.notes: Serial link to the host (G-code sender). Broken out on the shield RX/TX header. Leave free.

pins.label: D2

functions.name: A.STEP when the A axis is jumpered to clone X

pins.notes: Same in all GRBL versions.

pins.label: D3

functions.name: A.STEP when the A axis is jumpered to clone Y

pins.notes: Same in all GRBL versions.

pins.label: D4

functions.name: A.STEP when the A axis is jumpered to clone Z

pins.notes: Same in all GRBL versions.

pins.label: D5

functions.name: A.DIR when the A axis is jumpered to clone X

pins.notes: Same in all GRBL versions.

pins.label: D6

functions.name: A.DIR when the A axis is jumpered to clone Y

pins.notes: Same in all GRBL versions.

pins.label: D7

functions.name: A.DIR when the A axis is jumpered to clone Z

pins.notes: Same in all GRBL versions.

pins.label: D8

functions.name: EN (stepper enable/disable, shared by all four drivers)

pins.notes: One enable line for all drivers. The shield has a 10 kΩ pull-up from EN to 5 V ("Disable Drivers" in the schematic), so the drivers stay disabled until GRBL drives this pin. Same in all GRBL versions.

pins.label: D9

functions.name: X limit (shield X+ and X- end-stop pins)

pins.notes: Input, held high by the internal pull-up (Protoneer pin layout). X+ and X- share this one pin. Same in all GRBL versions.

pins.label: D10

functions.name: Y limit (shield Y+ and Y- end-stop pins)

pins.notes: Input, held high by the internal pull-up (Protoneer pin layout). Y+ and Y- share this one pin. Same in all GRBL versions.

pins.label: D11

functions.name: Spindle PWM / spindle enable (GRBL 0.9/1.1 default, variable spindle)

pins.notes: Wired to the shield end-stop pins silkscreened "Z+ / Z-". GRBL 0.9 and 1.1 default builds (VARIABLE_SPINDLE on) use this pin for the spindle PWM/enable output, so connect your spindle speed signal here, NOT a Z limit switch. GRBL 0.8c (or builds with VARIABLE_SPINDLE off): Z limit input.

pins.label: D12

functions.name: A.STEP when the A axis is jumpered to D12

pins.notes: Wired to the shield pin silkscreened "SpnEn". GRBL 0.9 and 1.1 default builds use it as the Z limit input, so wire the Z limit switch to the SpnEn pin. GRBL 0.8c (or VARIABLE_SPINDLE off): spindle enable output. Also selectable as A.STEP with the A-axis jumper, which then conflicts with the GRBL function.

pins.label: D13

functions.name: A.DIR when the A axis is jumpered to D13

pins.notes: Wired to the shield pin silkscreened "SpnDir". Spindle direction in GRBL 0.8c, 0.9 and 1.1. If GRBL 1.1 is compiled with USE_SPINDLE_DIR_AS_ENABLE_PIN, this pin becomes spindle enable instead. Also selectable as A.DIR with the A-axis jumper.

pins.label: A0
pins.notes: Shield pin "Abort". Input, held high by the internal pull-up (Protoneer pin layout). Same in GRBL 0.8c and 1.1.

pins.label: A1

functions.name: Safety door (only if GRBL is built with ENABLE_SAFETY_DOOR_INPUT_PIN)

pins.notes: Shield pin "Hold". Input, held high by the internal pull-up (Protoneer pin layout). Same in GRBL 0.8c and 1.1.

pins.label: A2
pins.notes: Shield pin "Resume". Input, held high by the internal pull-up (Protoneer pin layout). Same in GRBL 0.8c and 1.1.

pins.label: A3
pins.notes: Shield pin "CoolEn". Output. Same in GRBL 0.8c and 1.1.

pins.label: A4

functions.name: Coolant mist (M7), only if GRBL 1.1 is built with ENABLE_M7

pins.notes: Broken out on the shield I2C header (labelled A4/SDA). Unused by GRBL 0.8c and by default GRBL 1.1 builds (ENABLE_M7 is off by default).

pins.label: A5
pins.notes: Broken out on the shield I2C header (labelled A5/SCL); the V3.xx schematic has no separate probe connector. GRBL 0.9/1.1 read the touch probe here. Unused in GRBL 0.8c.

pins.label: 5V

functions.name: 5V (logic supply for the drivers, from the Uno)

pins.notes: Logic 5 V from the Uno feeds the drivers' VDD. Motor power comes from the separate 12-36 V screw terminal, never from this pin.

pins.label: GND
pins.notes: Common ground between the Uno, the shield and the motor supply.
